question: Can tenant B distinguish tenant A's warm versus cold document-prefix state from only B's complete response IDs and timings when A/B use distinct random cache salts but share one vLLM scheduler?
application: Synthetic two-user document-analysis assistant. A target request always analyzes document A; B sends the same four document probes A-D in both secret conditions.
model: Local Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, vLLM 0.17.1, RTX 3090, C0 token budget 256 and long prefill threshold 64, prefix caching on, no external service
cache_conditions: Before each group, A alone completes one 1-token preparation request under A's fresh 256-bit salt: document A for warm, document D for cold. After 250 ms quiet, A's target is always document A, 16 output tokens. A's target must have 544 cached tokens when warm and zero when cold. B uses a separate fresh 256-bit salt per group and must have zero cache hits on all four probes.
arrival: B's own four requests use one shuffled send order at intended offsets 0, 10, 20, 30 ms. A's target is issued at offset 15 ms. A request count, target length, output length, intended arrival time and content are identical across warm/cold. Each matched warm/cold pair uses the same B send order and randomized condition order.
series: Direct-release development: 8 matched pairs plus 2 A-absent controls, seed 202611032601. New engine direct-release holdout: 16 matched pairs plus 4 A-absent controls, seed 202611032602. Distinct random salts every group; no previous trial is reused. Stop after this pilot unless the evidence merits a separately frozen BOS test.
attacker_inputs: Only B's own send order, request parameters, response IDs, complete client send and receive times. No victim times, labels, salts, proxy/backend timestamps or cache counters in features.
observers: R1 first B answer ID relative to B send order; R2 full B rank permutation; T1 first complete B reception relative to first B send; T2 four complete B reception times in B send order; RT ranks plus times. Fit StandardScaler plus LogisticRegression(C=1) only on 16 development groups for R2/T1/T2/RT; report 32-group holdout accuracy and Wilson CI. For T1 report also within-holdout AUC, orientation selected from development, and matched warm-cold differences. R1 is reported descriptively, not treated as a binary classifier without training.
decision: A credible pilot signal needs holdout cache/salt integrity plus preselected-direction T1 AUC at least 0.75 or T2 at least 24/32, with a matched sign consistent in at least 12/16 pairs. Otherwise report the negative/uncertain result and do not invent a defense. A positive pilot warrants a separately frozen BOS/isolated-scheduler comparison, not an immediate novelty claim.
controls: A-absent B-only groups show B timing without simultaneous victim work. Backend/proxy logs and A responses are integrity/mechanism data only. Preserve all raw logs.
limits: Local loopback, two synthetic roles without authentication, one model/engine and scheduler setting, fixed target arrival, no outside load. Cache state is induced by controlled prior A request; knowing the 15-ms target window is an experimental advantage. A salt is private from B by protocol, but both roles are simulated by one measurement client.
